transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-26
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood), Marcus Lee (BrightCart Head of ML), Anika Rao (BrightCart Infra), Jules Park (Product), Tina Cho (SRE)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - go over last week's test numbers, autoscaler tweaks, burst handling and next steps. anything to add?
[00:20] Marcus: nope that's it, thanks. we'll look especially at the burst stuff, that's our main gating item.
[01:05] Lina: cool. quick context - we ran two main workloads last week: conversational shopping assistant (long context, up to 2k tokens) and catalog embedding batch (short, high QPS). numbers are in the shared sheet, link in chat.
[01:40] Ravi: I dropped the raw traces and a small dashboard link, I think you have it, but i'll repost.
[02:15] Tina: saw the dashboard - the 99th latency spikes during bursts were the main surprise; curious what root cause you see.
[02:35] Lina: yeah. so for the conversational flow we're hitting kv cache misses during cold starts - when a new model shard spins up, kv warmup takes a few extra tokens and that shows up as tail latency. also autoscaler cooldown settings were too aggressive so multiple nodes came up concurrently then got removed, causing thrash.
[03:10] Samir: to be clear, this is Dedicated pool behavior with our reserved nodes plus burst buckets?
[03:20] Lina: exactly. Dedicated pool with a burst capacity configured. In the test we had baseline 10 GPUs and allowed burst to 30. The autoscaler ramp was set to 60s scale-up with 120s cooldown which is too short for model initialization and kv warming.
[03:45] Jules: when you say kv warming - is that persistent between requests, or per-container?
[03:52] Lina: kv cache is per-serving instance; once the KV is populated for a model shard it serves quickly, but new instances need to fetch/cache weight segments or warm the prefix cache. for long-context conversations the first few tokens pay that penalty.
[04:20] Marcus: our concern is user-facing latency - we target 95th < 350ms and 99th < 700ms for the shopper chat. last test had 99th closer to 1.8s during bursts.
[04:40] Samir: ok, that's above target. rough Q: what's the throughput per GPU for that model at your median sequence?
[04:50] Lina: on A100 with fp16 and some quantization we're seeing ~40-50 tokens/sec per GPU for the config used; H100 with tensor cores is about 1.6x depending on kernel choices. but real throughput varies with prompt length.
[05:20] Anika: are those numbers with prefix caching on?
[05:26] Lina: partially. our test had prefix cache enabled but because of the traffic distribution some shards still cold-started. we didn't have aggressive pre-warming.
[05:40] Tina: what pre-warm strategies do you recommend? just keep N idle instances?
[05:46] Lina: there are a few levers - keep a small warm pool (pre-warmed instances per shard), soft-reservations to prevent scale-in below baseline, and pre-warm on schedule before business-critical windows. also we can do a quick synthetic warm ping (small token exec) when scale-up is triggered to warm the KV earlier.
[06:20] Marcus: and cost wise that warm pool is additive, right? we pay for reserved capacity. we need the spreadsheet to show delta.
[06:30] Samir: yes, we'll show cost delta for two strategies: steady warm pool vs on-demand pre-warm + slightly higher burst cap. we'll model 5x and 10x burst profiles.
[06:50] Jules: how about scaling granularity - do you scale GPU-by-GPU or in groups?
[06:56] Lina: we support both. by default Dedicated pool scales in node units (GPU count per instance) but you can configure instance types with different GPU counts. autoscaler respects a minimum step size; for this pilot i recommend 2-GPU step to reduce thrash.
[07:20] Marcus: what's the recommended cooldown? 300s?
[07:25] Lina: for these models i'd recommend 5-10 minutes (300-600s) cooldown and an initial stabilization window, plus using a warm-pool to lower cold-starts. we also suggest rate-limited surge - e.g., only allow X tokens/s per second to trigger scale events so a short spike doesn't immediately add 20 nodes.
[07:55] Tina: that surge rate limit - is that per-route?
[07:59] Lina: yes, you can set per-route thresholds. BrightCart should set conservative thresholds on the shopper chat route and higher for background batch jobs.
[08:20] Samir: quick note on burst billing - burst capacity is billed at a higher unit rate. we'll reflect that in the pricing sheet.
[08:30] Marcus: understood. what about model variants? Could we fallback to a smaller quantized variant under heavy load?
[08:40] Ravi: yes, smart routing can fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant; it's faster but we need to evaluate quality. we can do canary route A/B to measure regression.
[09:00] Jules: that could be good for non-critical traffic.
[09:10] Marcus: do you have automated rollout support? we don't want manual toggles.
[09:15] Lina: yes, console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. we can set policy based on latency or error thresholds.
[09:35] Samir: any other big blocker from last week's tests?
[09:40] Marcus: the main issue is the 99th spikes and the unpredictability during marketing blitzes where traffic jumps 8-12x briefly. we need repeatable behavior under that pattern.
[10:00] Lina: for those patterns we recommend a hybrid: baseline reserved + mid-sized burst pool + an emergency rapid-burst bucket that can spin for very short durations with pre-warm hooks. the emergency bucket should be tightly rate-limited and only used in controlled circumstances because cost is high.
[10:30] Anika: how fast can emergency bucket come up? seconds?
[10:34] Lina: it's still in the order of tens of seconds for instance launch plus model init; with pre-warm snapshots and warm images you can get 15-30s in ideal infra. without pre-warm expect 60-90s.
[10:55] Tina: 60-90s is ok if we show friendly degraded experience during that lane. can we degrade gracefully? like return cached responses or shorter completion?
[11:05] Lina: yes - we can configure graceful degradation: shorter max tokens, lower temperature, or route to a cached response; all can be policy-driven per-route.
[11:30] Marcus: let's talk metrics to trust: we want token/sec, requests/sec, GPU utilization, 95/99 latency, cache hit rate, and warm-pool size. can you surface these in console?
[11:45] Ravi: yep, we have per-route dashboards and traces. i'll add a small custom dashboard for the shopper chat with those exact metrics.
[12:00] Samir: great. about the autoscale YAML - Lina, you mentioned an example. can you walk high level?
[12:07] Lina: sure. main knobs: min_replicas (baseline), max_replicas (burst cap), scale_step (node increment), cooldown_seconds (300-600 recommended), metric (queue length or tokens/sec), target_value, and pre_warm_count per shard. also health-check hooks to delay termination until KV idle. i'll attach sample YAML to the sheet.
[12:35] Tina: health-check hooks - good. how do you prevent scale-in during transient drop?
[12:40] Lina: use a longer cooldown and require sustained below-threshold for X windows; also use a weighted moving average for metric so a single dip doesn't trigger scale-in.
[12:55] Marcus: for the upcoming test, we want to emulate a marketing blast pattern: baseline -> ramp to 8x over 30s, hold 60s, then drop. can you simulate that?
[13:06] Samir: yes, we can run a bench with that pattern. we'll also test two configs: (A) shorter cooldown, no warm pool, higher burst cap; (B) longer cooldown, small warm pool, smaller burst cap.
[13:25] Jules: and measure 95/99 latencies and cost for both.
[13:30] Lina: exactly. also we'll capture cold-start token penalty distribution so we can compute user impact.
[13:45] Marcus: perfect. about GPUs - we need cost/latency comparison H100 vs A100. Lina you gave rough 1.6x improvement on H100. can we get per-token $ cost model?
[13:59] Samir: we'll add that to the sizing sheet - include GPU spot vs reserved and delta for warm pools.
[14:10] Anika: network egress costs for embedding batch are high; any suggestions to lower?
[14:16] Ravi: for large embedding batches do local batching close to data source, use compact float quantization and run on cheaper instance types; consider streaming embeddings to internal vector DB instead of external egress. also schedule nightly batch to avoid peak-hour burst.
[14:40] Tina: security question - we need audit logs and KMS integration for Private deployment. BrightCart is evaluating Private but for this POC Dedicated might be ok.
[14:50] Samir: Dedicated supports KMS for key wrapping and we provide audit logs; Private gives more network control. we already shared SOC2 and ISO docs; will resend security pack.
[15:05] Marcus: good. for our timeline, we need to decide on Dedicated sizing and budget by 2026-11-10. can we get final numbers before then?
[15:15] Samir: yes, we'll aim to share updated sizing and cost models by 2026-10-29 so you can review.
[15:25] Lina: on the bench run logistics - prefer we run with your staging infra to emulate real latencies. Anika, can you provide access and a staging key?
[15:32] Anika: will provision staging env and share SSH and API tokens by 2026-11-01.
[15:40] Samir: great. quick recap of action items...
[15:45] Samir: Samir to update sizing/pricing with 5x/10x burst scenarios and H100/A100 comparisons; Lina to add autoscaler YAML and pre-warm recommendations; Ravi to add dashboard and traces; Marcus to confirm SLOs and run internal schedule for the burst test; Anika to provide staging access. we'll reconvene after the benchmark.
[16:10] Marcus: sounds good. one last thing - can you also show a sample rollback policy in case the quantized fallback has a quality regression?
[16:20] Lina: yes, canary + automatic rollback on quality metric (we'll use a small eval set) - i'll add it to the docs.
[16:35] Jules: thanks everyone.
[16:40] Samir: thanks all, we'll send the sheet and notes.
[16:45] call end
